title: Choricius of Gaza, Orations I–VIII (Laudationes Marciani I–II, Laudatio Aratii et Stephani, Laudatio Summi, Epithalamia, Epitaphioi for Maria and Procopius) / Хорикий Газский, Речи
author: Choricius of Gaza
genre: Epideictic oratory: encomia (with church ekphrasis), wedding speeches, funeral orations
edition: Foerster & Richtsteig, Choricii Gazaei opera (Teubner 1929, repr. 1972); 1929 imprint is US public domain. Boissonade 1846 (public domain, partial corpus): archive.org/details/choriciigazaeio00boisgoog
ru_evidence: Russian Wikipedia 'Хорикий Газский' lists only the Apologia mimorum (Freyberg 1968) and the Brumalia speech (Bolgov 2016), and states that no work has a complete Russian translation. Orations I–VIII are absent.
en_evidence: BMCR 2010.10.02: Penella 2009 translates only the declamations and dialexeis; the eight orations are not in it. Litsas 1980 is an unpublished Chicago dissertation (scope unverified).
other_translations: Italian: Or. VII–VIII by C. Greco 2010 (BMCR 2011.12.41); Or. VIII also by Corcella in Amato (ed.) 2010. French or German for Or. I–VI: none found.
value: Main literary source for 6th-century Gaza: ekphraseis of the churches of St Sergius and St Stephen (art history, archaeology, mosaics), civic and episcopal elite, Christian sophistic under Justinian. Used by Byzantinists, art historians and historians of rhetoric. No Russian and no published English.
ai_feasibility: Medium-high. Atticist prose, dense allusion and ekphrastic and architectural terms. Penella's version of the declamations helps calibrate style. Architectural vocabulary needs expert review.
pilot_unit: Laudatio Marciani I (Or. I), including the St Sergius ekphrasis; estimated about 7,000 words.
